## What Problem This Solves
Channel-self-delivered sends (native auto-replies) bypass core `deliverOutboundPayloads`, so the canonical `message:sent` event never fires and `message:sent` consumers (the `message_sent` plugin hook + the internal `message:sent` hook) are blind to them despite successful delivery. ## Why This Change Was Made
Core owns the canonical `message.sent` emission; extensions need a narrow, generic, supported way to report a delivery they performed without reaching into core hook internals. This adds one shared core emitter (`emitCanonicalMessageSent`) that both the explicit-send path and the new seam route through, so the two emission sites cannot drift in hook order or gating.

## User Impact
Plugins/consumers observing `message_sent` / internal `message:sent` now also observe channel-self-delivered messages (e.g. delivery logs, responded-accounting, watchdogs). The explicit-send path is unchanged. Additive and fail-open — no change to delivery behavior or config.

## Summary

Signal native replies now preserve quote metadata across durable delivery, direct outbound sends, queued recovery, and unknown-send reconciliation. Signal direct replies derive the native quote author from the normalized target, while group/durable replies carry inbound sender metadata when the reply still targets the current inbound message.

The PR also closes the retargeting edge cases around native replies: explicit `replyToId` beats inline reply directives, single-use implicit replies consume the id and author together, and payloads that retarget a different reply id do not inherit a stale ambient quote author.

## What Changed

- Signal send surfaces: message adapter text/media, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media forward `replyToId` and `replyToAuthor` into Signal send options.
- Durable delivery and queue recovery: core send contexts, durable delivery, queue storage/replay, and unknown-send reconciliation preserve optional `replyToAuthor` alongside `replyToId`.
- Reply routing rules: explicit `replyToId` now wins over parsed inline `[[reply_to:...]]` directives, and ambient reply authors are cleared when the effective reply id no longer matches the original reply target.
- Plugin SDK contract: the outbound context API baseline hash is regenerated for the intentional optional `replyToAuthor` send-context field.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal sends using `signal:u:Alice` normalize the send target and derived native quote author to `username:alice`.
- Durable Signal replies pass native quote metadata through message adapter, formatted, attached-result, queued recovery, and unknown-send reconciliation paths.
- Reconciled recovery commit hooks receive `replyToAuthor` when the effective reply id still matches the queued reply id, and omit it when recovery retargeted to a different effective reply id.

target.title: fix(media): make wake-false direct fallback reason-aware
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#95910 tracks a focused follow-up to #86034: after successful media generation, `scheduleMediaGenerationTaskCompletion()` treated a `wakeTaskCompletion()` false return as an unconfirmed completion and closed the detached task as blocked, while the thrown wake path already had direct media recovery.

The unsafe fix would be to direct-send after every boolean `false`. That would recover some media-loss cases, but it also breaks the current no-send contract for `requester_abandoned` and unknown/generic false returns because the scheduler no longer knows why delivery failed.

This PR fixes that boundary by preserving the existing `wakeTaskCompletion(): Promise<boolean>` API and adding a media-internal detailed wake result so successful-generation closeout can still see the structured delivery reason before deciding whether direct fallback is allowed.

Fixes #95910.
Partial follow-up for #86034.
Supersedes the unsafe fallback boundary in #95945.

## Summary

- keeps the existing `wakeTaskCompletion(): Promise<boolean>` API for current media/tool callers
- adds a media-internal detailed wake result for scheduler closeout
- retries direct media delivery only for recoverable media-loss reasons:
  - `generated_media_missing`
  - `message_tool_delivery_missing`
  - `visible_reply_missing`
- keeps `requester_abandoned`, generic/no-reason false returns, and terminal delivery stops as no-send blocked outcomes
- adds scheduler-level regression coverage for the allowed reason, requester-abandoned, generic false, and thrown wake paths

## Behavior Matrix

| wake result | direct fallback? | terminal result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| delivered | no extra fallback | success |
| `generated_media_missing` / `message_tool_delivery_missing` / `visible_reply_missing` | yes, if direct channel origin is deliverable | clears blocked result on success |
| `requester_abandoned` | no | blocked |
| no reason / generic false | no | blocked |
| terminal delivery stop | no | handled as before |
| thrown wake after successful generation | existing direct recovery path remains | clears blocked result on success |

## Evidence

Local validation from this branch:

- Installed dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; lockfile was unchanged.
- Formatting check passed:
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts`
- Relevant Vitest set passed: 5 files, 143 tests.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts src/agents/tools/image-generate-background.test.ts src/agents/tools/video-generate-background.test.ts src/agents/tools/music-generate-background.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- TypeScript core check passed:
  - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- Narrow lint passed:
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.ts src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts`
- Whitespace check passed:
  - `git diff --check`

Regression coverage added in `src/agents/tools/media-generate-background-shared.test.ts`:

- detailed false with `generated_media_missing` and a deliverable origin calls direct fallback and clears `terminalResult`
- detailed false with `requester_abandoned` does not call `sendMessage` and remains blocked
- detailed false with no reason/generic error does not call `sendMessage` and remains blocked
- existing thrown wake direct recovery remains covered
- existing lifecycle-level tests still cover direct fallback through the old boolean wrapper and no-send behavior for requester abandonment/generic handoff failure

Mantis Telegram Desktop proof was attempted in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28294989921. The harness validated the selected refs, but the agentic Telegram proof job failed because the available Telegram setup could not reproduce the required generated-media completion wake-false condition. The uploaded `mantis-evidence.json` reported both baseline and candidate as `skipped`, with no video/artifacts produced.

That Mantis result is not behavioral proof that this PR works, and it is also not evidence that the candidate failed. It shows the current visible Telegram proof harness cannot trigger this internal delivery-result path. Current evidence remains the mocked scheduler and delivery-path coverage for the exact delivery-policy matrix changed by this PR.

Live gateway/channel proof remains open unless maintainers accept the scheduler boundary proof for this internal failure mode or provide/approve a live hook that can inject a recoverable `SubagentAnnounceDeliveryResult` such as `generated_media_missing` against a real channel.

target.title: fix(infra): clarify Allow Always unavailable message for one-shot commands
target.body:
## Summary

- When Allow Always is unavailable due to the command's shell redirection or runtime payload (not because the policy is ask=always), the approval prompt now explains the actual reason.
- Previously, commands like `openclaw --version 2>&1` would show "The effective approval policy requires approval every time" even when the effective policy was ask=on-miss.
- Fix: check if `ask === "always"` before using the policy-related message; otherwise use the command-shape explanation.

## Root Cause

`buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` at `src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts:378` used a single generic message whenever `allow-always` was not in `allowedDecisions`. The actual reason could be either (a) the policy is `ask=always`, or (b) the command is one-shot (shell redirection / runtime payload prevents persistent approval). The message implied (a) in all cases, which was misleading.

## Verification

- Code logic verified by reading the source: `params.ask` is available at the reply payload builder; `request.request.ask` is available at the forwarder message builder.
- When `ask === "always"`: preserves original accurate message.
- When `ask !== "always"` (e.g. "on-miss", "off", null): uses the new command-shape explanation.
- Test at `exec-approval-reply.test.ts:319` uses `ask: "always"` and continues to pass.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Approval prompt now shows accurate reason when Allow Always is unavailable for one-shot commands.

**Environment tested:** Source code analysis on OpenClaw main (Node 22, Linux).

**Steps run after the patch:** Traced the full approval-reply flow:

- `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` in `src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts`: when `ask` is not `"always"` and `allow-always` is unavailable, uses the command-shape explanation.
- `buildExecApprovalRequestMessage` in `src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts`: same differentiation via `request.request.ask`.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
Before:  "Allow Always is unavailable because the effective policy requires approval every time."
After:   "Allow Always is unavailable for this command. The command's shell redirection or runtime payload prevents persistent approval."
         (when the policy is NOT ask=always, e.g. ask=on-miss with one-shot command)
```

**Observed result after the fix:** Users running commands with shell redirection (`2>&1`, `2>/dev/null`) no longer see a misleading message claiming the policy requires approval every time when the actual effective policy is ask=on-miss.

**Not tested:** Live gateway session with real exec approval prompts. The change is a string-only message update with no behavioral logic change.

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

target.title: [codex] fix gateway hot-mode restart reloads
target.body:
## Summary

Closes the silent-staleness hole in `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"` without changing the shipped default contract. Hot mode keeps warn-and-keep for routine restart-required config edits; two scoped behaviors layer on top:

- **`gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired: true`** (new optional key, default `false`): opt-in that delegates restart-required edits to the gateway's existing idle-aware restart path, matching `mode: "hybrid"` for the restart-required branch while keeping hot-safe edits hot.
- **Security-critical carve-out** (always on): restart reasons under `gateway.auth.*`, `auth.profiles.*` / `auth.order.*`, and top-level `secrets.*` schedule a restart even in default hot mode. Without this, a `gateway.auth.token` rotation, a doctor batch that renames `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` profiles, or a `secrets.providers.*` change on disk sits behind warn-and-keep while the runtime keeps honoring the stale credential/profile state.

The hot-mode restart policy is one shared decision (`resolveHotModeRestartDecision`) used by both the file watcher and the `config.patch` / `config.apply` RPC write path, so the two write surfaces cannot diverge. **This changes current RPC behavior in hot mode**: previously `config.patch`/`config.apply` scheduled a direct restart for any restart-required write regardless of the opt-in; now routine restart-required RPC writes return a `requiresRestart` notice without bouncing the gateway (matching the watcher's warn-and-keep contract), while security-critical and opted-in writes still schedule the direct restart.

An earlier draft of this PR made hot mode schedule restarts unconditionally; review correctly flagged that as a semantic change to the shipped `hot` contract, and the current shape supersedes it. Existing `mode: "hot"` deployments are behavior-stable on upgrade for routine edits.

## Details

- `src/gateway/config-reload-settings.ts:32`: `SECURITY_CRITICAL_RESTART_PREFIXES = ["gateway.auth", "auth.profiles", "auth.order", "secrets"]`. The `auth.profiles` / `auth.order` entries fix the review-found P1: the production repro (doctor batch renaming `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` with model routes) produced restart reasons under `auth.profiles.*` / `auth.order.*`, which are unmatched in the reload-plan rules and default to restart-required — so default hot mode dropped them with a warn. The `secrets` prefix is top-level, fixing the earlier `gateway.secrets` prefix that could never match real restart reasons; `src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts` marks `secrets.providers.*` restart-required so the carve-out has a live trigger.
- `src/gateway/config-reload-settings.ts:54`: `resolveHotModeRestartDecision` returns `"security-critical" | "opt-in" | "warn-and-keep"` and is the single owner of the hot-mode policy.
- `src/gateway/config-reload.ts:319`: the watcher's restart-required hot branch routes through the shared decision; the existing idle-aware restart machinery (`queueRestart`) remains the only watcher restart path.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts:178`: fixes the review-found P2 divergence — `resolveConfigRestartRequirement` now routes hot-mode RPC writes through the same decision instead of unconditionally direct-restarting (`scheduleDirectRestart: mode === "hot"`).
- `gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired` added to `src/config/types.gateway.ts`, `zod-schema.ts` (strict validation), `schema.help.ts`, `schema.labels.ts`.
- Regression tests pin each branch: warn-and-keep preserved on non-security edits; opt-in queues a supervised restart; security-critical auth/secrets changes restart regardless of the opt-in; the doctor-batch `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` rename auto-restarts in default hot mode (`src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts:1878`); and the RPC path is pinned three ways in `src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts:366-421` (routine write keeps running with `requiresRestart: true`, opt-in direct-restarts, auth-token write direct-restarts).
- Docs updated: `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md`, `docs/gateway/configuration.md`, `docs/gateway/index.md` describe the default, the opt-in, the carve-out, and that the policy applies to both file edits and `config.patch`/`config.apply` writes.

**Open maintainer decision:** this adds one config key on a compatibility-sensitive surface, and there is no maintainer sign-off yet on the `gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired` key. The default split (warn-and-keep stays default; auth-profile/auth/secrets changes always restart) is the proposed contract — if a different split is preferred (e.g. opt-in defaulting `true` for fresh installs only), say the word and I will adjust. The RPC alignment above is also a deliberate behavior change to today's hot-mode `config.patch` direct-restart; if maintainers prefer the RPC surface to keep direct-restarting unconditionally, that is a one-line revert in `resolveConfigRestartRequirement`.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: in hot reload mode, a config write touching any restart-required key was dropped with a single `log.warn` while the gateway kept serving from the stale in-memory snapshot. Observed in production as a 4-hour silent outage where the agent kept resolving the legacy `openai-codex/gpt-5.5` model id after `openclaw doctor --fix` had migrated the on-disk config (including `auth.profiles.openai-codex:*` renames) to `openai/gpt-5.5`; group messages silently dropped, admin DMs returned a canned `[agent failed]` reply. With this patch, security-critical edits (gateway auth, auth profiles/order, secrets) self-heal via restart by default, and operators can opt all restart-required edits into the same path.

- **Real environment tested**: isolated sandbox gateway on macOS (loopback port 28789), dist built from this branch at commit `d023afb9c4` (the commit introducing the opt-in + carve-out design); plus the original production incident capture on a launchd-supervised deployed gateway (`gateway-host`) documenting the pre-fix failure mode. The subsequent changes (top-level `secrets` prefix, `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` prefixes, shared RPC policy, rebase onto current main) are pinned by focused regression tests run locally at head `074e8acf36`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: sandbox scenarios (at `d023afb9c4`): start a fresh sandbox gateway from the branch dist, wait for the config watcher to settle, write one config edit, observe the reload log and process state.
  ```
  Scenario A: mode "hot" (defaults), edit gateway.bind "loopback" -> "lan"
  Scenario B: mode "hot" + autoRestartOnRequired true, same edit
  Scenario C: mode "hot" (defaults), rotate gateway.auth.token
  ```
  At final head `074e8acf36`:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**: redacted runtime log captured live from the sandbox gateway reload/restart console output (at `d023afb9c4`):
  ```
  A: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (gateway.bind)
     process state: RUNNING (pid=8610, uptime 00:14)        # warn-and-keep preserved
  B: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode scheduling restart per gateway.reload.autoRestartOnRequired=true (gateway.bind)
     [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
     [shutdown] started: gateway restarting
     process state: RUNNING (pid=6706, uptime 00:15)        # restarted clean
  C: [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode scheduling restart for security-critical change (gateway.auth.token)
     [gateway] received SIGUSR1; restarting
     process state: RUNNING (pid=9261, uptime 00:14)        # credential rotation propagated
  ```
  At final head `074e8acf36` (local, macOS, Node 24):
  ```
  Test Files  8 passed (8)
       Tests  474 passed (474)
  ```
  including the doctor-batch `auth.profiles`/`auth.order` watcher regression and the three hot-mode `config.patch` policy tests. `tsgo` core + core-test lanes and `oxfmt`/`oxlint` on touched files also pass.

- **Observed result after fix**: scenario A proves existing hot-mode deployments keep the shipped warn-and-keep contract with no restart. Scenario B proves the opt-in routes routine restart-required edits through the existing SIGUSR1 + clean-shutdown restart path. Scenario C proves auth rotations propagate by default, closing the credential-rotation-bypass gap. The production failure mode (`hot mode ignoring` on `auth.profiles.*` for 4 hours) is now closed at the exact prefix that caused it, pinned by the regression test at `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts:1878`.

- **What was not tested**: live sandbox-gateway captures were not re-run at the final head — the `secrets.providers.*` rotation and the doctor-batch `auth.profiles` rename scenarios are proven at head `074e8acf36` by focused regression tests only, not by a fresh end-to-end gateway capture; this is a known proof gap called out for review. Also untested: launchd auto-respawn end-to-end on hosts using `KeepAlive: { SuccessfulExit: false }` (see operator note below — the clean-exit hand-off needs a kickstart watcher on such hosts; not a regression, the pre-fix path also required manual intervention). The sandbox ran unmanaged (in-process restart mode); the managed-install launchd restart path is covered by existing integration tests.

## Operator note: launchd `SuccessfulExit=false` hosts

Hosts that set `KeepAlive: { Crashed=true, SuccessfulExit=false }` (to dodge an unrelated respawn cascade) will not auto-respawn after the restart hand-off's clean exit. The deployment fork pairs this with a 30s interval watchdog (`launchctl print` state AND port-binding check, then `launchctl kickstart -k`) — documented here so the gap flagged in review is paired with its operational answer. Hosts on default launchd `KeepAlive` semantics respawn normally and need nothing.

target.title: fix(openrouter): bound music SSE buffering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:**
  OpenRouter music generation streaming in `extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.ts`, specifically the SSE reader that accumulates audio and transcript deltas from `/chat/completions` responses.
- **Root cause, in product terms:**
  Root cause: the OpenRouter music SSE parser treated the external stream as trustworthy because it assumed every event would be newline-delimited soon and every audio/transcript delta would stay reasonably sized. Pending text was appended into an in-memory string until a newline arrived, while decoded audio buffers and transcript chunks were collected without cumulative byte accounting at the source of accumulation.
- **Why it matters / User impact:**
  A malformed or oversized OpenRouter stream could make an OpenClaw process retain unbounded memory before the stream completed or timed out, instead of failing with a clear provider error.
- **Fix classification:**
  Root-cause defensive bound on untrusted provider stream accumulation.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Complete shipped solution:**
  Added byte accounting at each accumulation point: a 2 MiB pending SSE event limit before appending decoded text, a 64 MiB cumulative decoded audio limit, and a 1 MiB cumulative transcript limit.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:**
  This fixes the root parser invariant because each guard is placed at the exact source of untrusted accumulation: raw bytes are counted before SSE text is appended to the pending line buffer, decoded audio bytes are counted before a buffer is retained, and transcript UTF-8 bytes are counted before a transcript chunk is retained. The fix therefore enforces the stream-size contract where memory growth originates instead of masking the symptom later at concat time or waiting for a timeout.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:**
  The limits are local OpenRouter music-provider stream safety constants. They do not change the plugin SDK contract, request schema, auth flow, model routing, or OpenRouter wire format.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:**
  Out of scope / unchanged: this PR does not change prompt construction, reference image handling, supported music models, output formats, provider configuration, auth, model routing, request schema, or non-music OpenRouter behavior. The change is only the local OpenRouter music stream safety boundary.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:**
  Valid streams under the caps continue to behave as before. Streams exceeding the caps now fail closed with explicit OpenRouter music generation errors.
- **Risk labels considered:**
  merge-risk:compatibility due to newly enforced fail-closed caps on very large provider streams.
- **Risk explanation:**
  The main behavior change is rejection of very large OpenRouter music responses: more than 64 MiB decoded audio, more than 1 MiB transcript text, or more than 2 MiB in a single unterminated SSE event.
- **Why acceptable:**
  These caps prevent unbounded memory growth from an external stream while preserving the existing API surface and normal chunked SSE behavior. The exact thresholds are intentionally provider-local safety bounds rather than SDK contract changes.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:**
  Receive deterministic provider failures for oversized or malformed OpenRouter music streams instead of exposing the process to unbounded buffering.
- **Existing behavior preserved:**
  Normal streaming audio chunks still concatenate in order, transcript chunks still join into lyrics, `[DONE]` still ends the stream, and existing reader cleanup behavior is preserved.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:**
  A successful live OpenRouter audio generation could not be completed from my available network exit: OpenRouter accepted the authenticated request path but returned provider HTTP 403 (`This model is not available in your region`) for the OpenRouter audio-output models tested. I am disclosing this as a live-proof limitation and requesting maintainer acceptance of the deterministic stream regression proof, or a maintainer-run live proof from a region where the models are available.

## Evidence

- **Environment:**
  Windows 10 / Git Bash workspace; repository test runner with the extension-providers Vitest project. Live OpenRouter attempts were run through the configured corporate HTTPS proxy after direct access to `openrouter.ai:443` timed out.
- **Commands run after this patch:**
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --project extension-providers extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.test.ts`

  Live-attempt command shape, with the API key supplied by environment and redacted in output:
  `HTTP_PROXY=http://proxyhk.zte.com.cn:80 HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxyhk.zte.com.cn:80 OPENROUTER_MUSIC_MODEL=<model> node --import tsx <redacted>/openrouter-music-live-proof.ts`
- **Key results / observations:**
  The focused OpenRouter music provider test command exited 0 after the final rebase onto current `origin/main`. The regression coverage includes: unterminated SSE event over 2 MiB, cumulative decoded audio over 64 MiB across multiple SSE events, and transcript text over 1 MiB.

  Redacted live OpenRouter attempts reached provider auth/request handling but were region-blocked by OpenRouter before an SSE audio stream was available:

  ```text
  model=google/lyria-3-clip-preview
  [live-proof] provider=openrouter envKeys=1 resolvedAuth=env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY key=[redacted suffix=49df] shellEnv=none
  [live-proof] starting generateMusic model=google/lyria-3-clip-preview format=mp3 durationSeconds=5 instrumental=true
  [live-proof] failed: ProviderHttpError: OpenRouter music generation failed (HTTP 403): This model is not available in your region.
  EXIT=1

  model=google/lyria-3-pro-preview
  [live-proof] provider=openrouter envKeys=1 resolvedAuth=env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY key=[redacted suffix=49df] shellEnv=none
  [live-proof] starting generateMusic model=google/lyria-3-pro-preview format=mp3 durationSeconds=5 instrumental=true
  [live-proof] failed: ProviderHttpError: OpenRouter music generation failed (HTTP 403): This model is not available in your region.
  EXIT=1

  model=openai/gpt-audio-mini
  [live-proof] provider=openrouter envKeys=1 resolvedAuth=env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY key=[redacted suffix=49df] shellEnv=none
  [live-proof] starting generateMusic model=openai/gpt-audio-mini format=mp3 durationSeconds=5 instrumental=true
  [live-proof] failed: ProviderHttpError: OpenRouter music generation failed (HTTP 403): This model is not available in your region.
  EXIT=1
  ```
- **Review findings addressed, if any:**
  ClawSweeper requested real OpenRouter proof. I attempted real authenticated OpenRouter calls after this patch and added the redacted output above. The remaining gap is environmental/provider-region availability, not an unattempted proof path; maintainers may still require a successful generation from an allowed region.

  RF-001: Addressed as far as the current environment allows. Redacted terminal output from authenticated OpenRouter calls is included above.
  RF-002: Disclosed live behavior proof limitation. The provider accepted auth and reached OpenRouter, but OpenRouter returned region 403 before an SSE audio stream was available.
  RF-003: Disclosed fail-closed compatibility risk for the new caps and kept deterministic stream regression coverage for the exact accumulation paths.
  RF-004: Requests explicit proof waiver or maintainer-side live proof from an allowed OpenRouter region because contributor-side successful generation is region-blocked.
  RF-005: Confirms the remaining blocker is maintainer acceptance of the proof limitation / fail-closed caps, not a code repair still pending in this PR.
- **Regression guardrail:**
  Regression test plan: the focused provider test file adds three stream-parser tests for the exact memory-growth paths. One test feeds an SSE event that never emits a newline and exceeds 2 MiB, one test sends multiple valid SSE audio events whose cumulative decoded audio exceeds 64 MiB, and one test sends transcript data exceeding 1 MiB. These unit regression tests are the smallest reliable guardrail because they exercise `readOpenRouterAudioStream`/`processOpenRouterSseLine` deterministically without depending on external model availability.
- **Patch quality notes:**
  Diff is limited to `extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.ts` and its provider test file. No lockfiles, generated files, or unrelated formatting changes are intended. Patch quality warning review: the added `catch` blocks preserve the existing reader cleanup lifecycle by cancelling/releasing the stream on error; they do not swallow provider errors or convert them into fallback/default success. Related PR scan: #98351 touches OpenRouter provider parsing but only guards malformed JSON; it does not address SSE pending bytes, cumulative decoded audio, or transcript caps.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:**
  High for the targeted memory-safety fix based on deterministic current-head stream tests and confirmed `origin/main` overlap checks. Live generation success remains unavailable from my current OpenRouter region, so the fail-closed caps need maintainer acceptance or maintainer-side live proof from an allowed region.

target.title: fix(trajectory): record session.ended after cleanup so its timestamp reflects actual session end time
target.body:
Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102014

**What Problem This Solves**
`session.ended` trajectory events always had the same timestamp as `model.completed`, making it impossible to measure actual session duration vs model compute time or detect cleanup delays from traces.

**Why This Change Was Made**
`session.ended` was recorded inline after `model.completed` in the same `try` block, both using `new Date().toISOString()` — they fired within the same microtask, before any cleanup ran. This fix moves `session.ended` recording to the `finally` block, after all resource cleanup completes, so the timestamp reflects the true wall-clock end time of the session lifecycle.

**Real Behavior Proof**

1. **Timestamp mechanism proof:** The trajectory runtime records event timestamps at `recordEvent` time via `new Date().toISOString()` (`src/trajectory/runtime.ts:547`). Moving the `session.ended` call from inline before cleanup to after cleanup in the `finally` block guarantees a later wall-clock timestamp.

2. **Regression test:** A focused test `"records session.ended timestamp later than model.completed when recorded after a delay"` was added at `src/trajectory/runtime.test.ts:517`. It uses `vi.useFakeTimers` + `vi.advanceTimersByTime(500)` to simulate the cleanup delay between `model.completed` and `session.ended`, then asserts `sessionEndedTs > modelCompletedTs` — proving the mechanism works correctly.

3. **Test results:**
   ```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  17 passed (17)
   ```

4. **Build:** `pnpm build` passes (exit code 0).

5. **Conflict resolution:** Rebased on latest `origin/main` at commit `ba514ea17`. The `timedOutByRunBudget` field is preserved in the deferred `session.ended` payload.

**User Impact**
Trajectory traces now show the real session end time. Operators can measure cleanup duration, distinguish model compute time from total session time, and build accurate session-latency dashboards.

**AI disclosure**
This PR was authored by Claude Code (Claude Fable 5) based on issue #102014.

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix(sdk): preserve zero sequence values in normalized gateway event IDs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SDK event normalization drops protocol-valid `seq: 0` and `ts: 0` from
normalized event IDs because `.filter(Boolean)` treats numeric zero as
falsy. This weakens event replay/dedupe identity for zero-sequence
gateway events.

Fixes #101768.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeGatewayEvent()` in `packages/sdk/src/normalize.ts` builds event
IDs from `[event.seq, event.event, runId, sessionKey, ts]` and applies
`.filter(Boolean)` before joining. The gateway protocol schema allows
`seq` as an integer with `minimum: 0`, so zero is a valid value.

The fix replaces `.filter(Boolean)` with `.filter((v) => v != null && v !== "")`,
preserving finite zero values while still omitting absent optional parts.

## Evidence

### Test results (Vitest)

```
$ npx vitest run packages/sdk/src/normalize.test.ts --no-coverage

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Duration  2.39s
```

2 regression tests added:
- `seq: 0` survives in the normalized ID
- `ts: 0` survives as the last ID part

## Merge Risk

Low. Single-line change in a pure string-building function. The
`.filter()` replacement preserves the existing behavior for all non-zero
values and empty strings.

target.title: fix(agents): keep chunkString and buildResumeMessage truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two UTF-16 truncation sites in the agent runtime that could produce broken U+FFFD replacement characters:

1. **`chunkString`** (`src/agents/bash-tools.shared.ts`) — splits large bash exec output into 8192-code-unit chunks for transport. Emoji crossing the chunk boundary gets split into a lone surrogate.

2. **`buildResumeMessage`** (`src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.ts`) — truncates subagent task descriptions at 2000 code units when building the resume message after gateway restart. Emoji at the boundary produces a broken character.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`chunkString`**: Replace `input.slice(i, i + limit)` with `sliceUtf16Safe(input, i, i + limit)` using the existing helper already imported in the same file.
- **`buildResumeMessage`**: Replace `task.slice(0, maxTaskLen)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(task, maxTaskLen)`.

## User Impact

- Bash exec output chunking no longer corrupts emoji at chunk boundaries during transport.
- Subagent resume messages after gateway restart display clean task descriptions without broken characters.

## Evidence

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.shared.test.ts src/agents/task-resume-utf16-safe.test.ts src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.test.ts

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  33 passed (33)
```

### Standalone production-path proof

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-chunk-resume-utf16-safe.mjs
node=v22.22.0  head=<PR-head-sha>
--- chunkString ---
inputCodeUnits=8194  beforeFix_surrogateAt8191=U+d83d
afterFix_chunks=2  chunkHasLoneSurrogate=false  dataPreserved=true
--- buildResumeMessage ---

afterFix_truncatedLen=1999  hasLoneSurrogate=false
result=PASS
```

### Files Changed (4 files, +86/-5)

```

 src/agents/subagent-orphan-recovery.ts |  3 +-

```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (Yes/No)
Yes. Bash exec output chunks and subagent resume messages no longer emit U+FFFD for emoji-boundary text.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (Yes/No)
No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (Yes/No)
No.

Agent bash exec output chunking and subagent orphan recovery message formatting.

How is that risk mitigated?
Both changes reuse the existing `sliceUtf16Safe`/`truncateUtf16Safe` helper with established test coverage. For ordinary input (no emoji at boundary), chunk sizes and content are identical to the old behavior. Existing tests (30 cases) pass without changes.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: Harden jq safe-bin semantics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators can explicitly configure exec safe bins for narrow stdin-oriented tools. `jq` is broader than that model: it can read environment data and load jq code through explicit modules and startup files, which means approval-free safe-bin execution cannot be constrained to the intended stdin-only behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes `jq` fail closed in the safe-bin semantic gate, matching the existing treatment for other tools whose semantics cannot be validated to stdin-only. Doctor and security audit now warn about jq/risky safe-bin entries without scaffolding profiles that can never satisfy the runtime semantic gate.

Operators can still run jq through an explicit allowlist entry or the normal approval prompt.

## User Impact

`jq` commands no longer qualify for approval-free execution through `tools.exec.safeBins`, even for simple field filters. Configurations that intentionally rely on jq should use an explicit allowlist entry for the trusted jq path or allow the approval prompt. Other safe-bin tools such as `head`, `tail`, `tr`, and `wc` are unchanged.

target.title: fix(googlechat): media downloads can grow unbounded without a size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where direct callers of the Google Chat media download API could omit `maxBytes` and let a successful media response buffer through an uncapped `arrayBuffer()` call. The normal inbound attachment path already passes a configured cap, but the exported helper still had an uncapped fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Chat media downloads now use the existing 20 MiB Google Chat media default whenever callers do not provide a stricter cap. Existing callers that pass `maxBytes` keep their configured limit and the existing `Google Chat media exceeds max bytes (...)` error contract.

The fallback is fixed at the helper boundary because omitted `maxBytes` means the direct caller did not opt into a stricter call-specific cap. Normal inbound Google Chat attachment handling still passes the configured `mediaMaxMb` value explicitly.

## User Impact

Google Chat media downloads fail closed instead of risking unbounded memory growth from an oversized media response. Operators who lower `mediaMaxMb` or callers that pass a stricter `maxBytes` still get the stricter limit.

## Evidence

- Source proof on current `main`: `downloadGoogleChatMedia` can call `fetchBuffer` without `maxBytes`; `fetchBuffer` then falls back to `Response.arrayBuffer()` on successful responses.
- Local focused test: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts -- --run` -> 1 file / 26 tests passed.
- Local format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts` -> clean.
- Local lint: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts` -> clean.
- Testbox-through-Crabbox: `tbx_01kwec4jk538eagta0w1ey5wk0` / Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28503690600 ran the focused Google Chat target test and `check:changed` successfully (`exitCode=0`).
- Regression proof now includes a controlled loopback HTTP endpoint streaming a chunked 32 MiB response through the real `downloadGoogleChatMedia` helper path; omitted `maxBytes` rejects at the 20 MiB default, invokes the guard release, and stops before the full payload is sent. It also proves Content-Length fast-fail without body reads and preserves explicit `maxBytes: 10` overflow text/cancellation.

target.title: fix(agents): keep tool-result truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted with Codex; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- Tool-result truncation now preserves UTF-16 boundaries when capping single results, detecting important error tails, and producing aggregate elision markers.
- Uses the existing `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` helpers (`sliceUtf16Safe` / `truncateUtf16Safe`) instead of raw string slicing.
- Intentionally out of scope: unrelated truncation sites, response-read bounding, config changes, and behavior outside this specific formatting boundary.

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- Related to the existing OpenClaw UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern (follow-up to Alix-007's merged UTF-16 campaign).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed:** Tool-result truncation preserves UTF-16 boundaries when capping single results, detecting important error tails, and producing aggregate elision markers.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0; PR head e050e018ff.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx` directly drives the exported truncation functions and checks for lone surrogates; plus `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal capture from the current PR branch shows the affected paths no longer return a lone surrogate.

```text
$ node --import tsx -e '<drive truncateToolResultText + truncateToolResultMessage on emoji-crossing-boundary inputs>'
simple truncation lone surrogate: false
head+tail truncation lone surrogate: false
head+tail truncation keeps error: true
message truncation lone surrogate: false

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
...
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 59 passed (59)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** the affected tool-result truncation paths keep output well-formed at the emoji/surrogate-pair boundary and preserve existing truncation markers, caps, and error-tail detection.
- **What was not tested:** full production deployment and unrelated provider/channel end-to-end delivery were not run; this proof is scoped to the touched local runtime path.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** no private credentials or live third-party service were required; proof uses local runtime execution and focused regression coverage for this formatting bug.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged):** raw JavaScript string slicing can cut between a high and low surrogate at these boundaries, which produces a malformed dangling surrogate in tool output/prompts.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts`
- Added focused regression coverage for the UTF-16 boundary case (simple truncation and head+tail error preservation).
- No known local failures from this change.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Malformed truncated tool output is now avoided while preserving existing caps and truncation markers.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No.

What is the highest-risk area?

agent tool-result formatting.

How is that risk mitigated?

The patch is limited to the existing truncation boundaries and is covered by focused regression proof above.

ClawSweeper re-review and maintainer review after this proof/body refresh.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

Nothing is waiting on the author after this proof update; waiting on CI/ClawSweeper/maintainer review.

target.title: feat(sandbox): add skipSkillsSync config option to suppress skill sync
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Skills are copied into the sandbox workspace on every sandbox setup. For users who do not use skills or have already preinstalled them in their sandbox Docker image, this sync is unnecessary overhead and adds startup latency. Related: #97638 ## Why This Change Was Made Adds `skipSkillsSync` as an optional boolean under `agents.defaults.sandbox` and `agents.list[].sandbox`, defaulting to `false`. When enabled: 1. **File copying skipped**: `syncSkillsToWorkspace` is not called — no skill files are copied into the sandbox workspace. 2. **Skill eligibility preserved**: `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` still runs; remote skill eligibility is advertised in agent prompts. 3. **Safe name-only prompt**: A new `SkillSnapshot` is built from `resolvedSkills` with sandbox-agnostic name-only entries (no host `` paths). Skill names are XML-escaped. The `skills` array is preserved for env overrides. 4. **Command prompt guard**: When `skipSkillsSync=true`, the command/system-prompt skill inspection returns empty early, preventing fallthrough to host-path-based snapshot resolution. ## User Impact ```json5 { agents: { defaults: { sandbox: { skipSkillsSync: true, docker: { setupCommand: "mkdir -p /workspace/skills && cp -r /preloaded-skills/* /workspace/skills/" } } } } } ``` Safe-use contract: Skills must be preinstalled in the sandbox via `docker.setupCommand` or `docker.binds`. The workspace bind-mount at `/workspace` shadows image-baked content, so skills baked directly at `/workspace/skills/` in a custom Docker image will not survive the mount. Use a separate path (e.g., `/preloaded-skills/`) and copy via `setupCommand`. ## Evidence ### Real behavior proof (Docker container) *Screenshot: terminal output from container with commit `e79a716ebe3`.* ``` ====================================================== Real Behavior Proof: skipSkillsSync Feature Container: openclaw-sandbox-test:latest Commit: e79a716ebe3 ====================================================== >>> 1. Config: skipSkillsSync=true { "agents": { "defaults": { "sandbox": { "mode": "all", "skipSkillsSync": true } } } } >>> 2. Sandbox explain: mode=all, sandboxed=true mode: all sandboxed: True >>> 3. Unit tests: 9 passed Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 9 passed (9) >>> 4. Code behavior: all OK SandboxConfig type : OK Config resolver : OK computeSkillsEligibility : OK Context branching : OK Name-only prompt (no paths) : OK XML escaping : OK Command prompt guard : OK Workspace info propagation : OK CLI runner propagation : OK Config labels : OK FIELD_HELP : OK Config baseline : OK Docs : OK ====================================================== ALL VERIFICATIONS PASSED ====================================================== ``` ### Test coverage (9 tests pass, 0 failures) - drops host snapshot and builds name-only prompt when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled - drops host snapshot (no remapping) when `skipSkillsSync` is absent (regression guard) - keeps snapshots for non-sandboxed runs (regression guard) - eligibility preserved in sandbox prompts (regression guard) - rebuilds sandbox prompts from materialized skill paths - preserves remote eligibility when rebuilding sandbox prompts - falls back to effective workspace for older sandbox contexts - escapes XML-special characters in skill names when `skipSkillsSync` is enabled - maps materialized read paths while preserving original file identities ### Changed files (12 files) | File | Change | |------|--------| | `src/config/types.agents-shared.ts` | Type definition for `skipSkillsSync` | | `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Zod schema with safe-use contract | | `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | Config UI labels | | `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Config help text | | `src/agents/sandbox/types.ts` | `SandboxConfig.skipSkillsSync` + `SandboxWorkspaceInfo.skipSkillsSync` | | `src/agents/sandbox/config.ts` | Config resolver propagation | | `src/agents/sandbox/context.ts` | Extracted `computeSandboxSkillsEligibility` helper + branching | | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.ts` | Name-only prompt + XML escaping when `skipSkillsSync` | | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sandbox-skills.test.ts` | 4 new test cases (9 total) | | `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts` | Pass `skipSkillsSync` to sandbox context | | `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-system-prompt.ts` | Early return guard against host snapshot fallthrough | | `docs/gateway/sandboxing.md` | Document `skipSkillsSync` in Skills Note | | `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` | Regenerated baseline |

target.title: feat(training-export): overhaul trigger system and message conversion
target.body:
> **Draft / work-in-progress** — this PR is under active development. Feedback welcome on the overall direction.

## Summary

Introduce a **trajectory-first, trigger-driven training export system** that produces episode-level JSONL data from the OpenClaw runtime — no offline reconstruction, no separate pipeline. The system is **opt-in** (`trainingExport.enabled: true`) and writes to:

```
~/.openclaw/training-export/episodes.jsonl
```

Each line is a self-contained training sample: a **task episode** (full agent turn with system prompt, messages, tools, metadata) or a **compact-summary episode** (compression prompt → summary pair for RL compaction training).

## Relationship to Existing Systems

### `/export-trajectory` (human-facing debug bundles)

The existing `/export-trajectory` command (docs at `docs/tools/trajectory.md`) produces **redacted interactive support bundles** for human debugging — prompt timelines, tool traces, transcript snapshots, usage metadata. It is triggered manually by users or support staff.

The training export introduced here is **complementary and non-overlapping**:

| | `/export-trajectory` | Training Export |
|---|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Human debugging, support | Machine training data |
| **Trigger** | Manual command | Automatic (compaction, reset, export command) |
| **Output** | Redacted bundle directory | JSONL episodes |
| **Format** | Directory of text/markdown files | One JSON line per episode |
| **Privacy** | Redacted (best-effort) | Full content (machine-consumed; opt-in) |
| **Audience** | Developers, support | RL training pipelines |

Both systems **read from the same trajectory** (trajectory capture / `cache-trace`). Training export simply produces a different output format for a different consumer, alongside the existing mechanism.

### Compaction subsystem

Training export hooks into the Pi SDK compaction lifecycle (`session_before_compact` + `session_compact`) to capture:
- **Pre-compaction context** (task episode): the full conversation before compression
- **Post-compaction summary** (summary episode): the prompt sent to the summarization model + the summary it produced, with `compaction` metadata (`tokensBefore`, `firstKeptEntryId`, `fromExtension`)

This is the same data the compaction system already computes internally — training export just persists it in a structured training format before it is discarded.

## Key Design Decisions

### 1. Trajectory-first
All training fields (system prompt, messages, tools, model metadata) come from runtime trajectory `context.compiled` events. Message and tool conversion delegates to the Pi SDK / provider layer (`convertMessages` from `@mariozechner/pi-ai/openai-completions`).

### 2. Unified compaction hook
A single Pi SDK extension (`session_before_compact` + `session_compact`) handles **all** compaction modes (default, safeguard, manual, overflow, timeout). No `runTrainingExport` calls scattered across individual compaction paths.

### 3. Pair-export guarantee
For compaction-triggered exports, task and summary episodes are built as a batch. If either is filtered by quality checks, **the entire batch is discarded** — no orphaned episodes.

### 4. Config-gated at every call site
`getTrainingExportConfig(cfg)?.enabled === true` is checked at all three entry points (extension registration, session reset, trajectory export command), so reviewers can see the opt-in gating logic without digging into implementation details.

### 5. `compactionSummary` bridging
Pi SDK's `convertToLlm` converts `compactionSummary` → `user` messages, but the upstream `convertMessages` from `@mariozechner/pi-ai/openai-completions` does not handle the `compactionSummary` role. A pre-processing step (sharing a single map with thinking-block stripping) mirrors Pi SDK's conversion format before handing off to the upstream converter.

### 6. Training-quality message filtering (all triggers)
Training episodes must end with a complete `assistant` message — regardless of trigger type. Any snapshot (compaction, reset, or trajectory export) may end mid-turn at a non-`assistant` message (e.g. `toolResult`). Trailing non-assistant messages are trimmed from every trigger's output. The `trainExampleMessagesAreUsable` check requires ≥1 user + ≥1 assistant; if trimming leaves the episode unusable, it is discarded entirely. This is a universal training-data quality requirement, not a compaction-specific behavior.

### 7. Reset export is independent of plugin hooks
The `before_reset` training export call is placed **outside** `emitGatewayBeforeResetPluginHook`, so it fires regardless of whether any `before_reset` plugin hooks are registered.

### 8. Private file permissions
The export directory (`~/.openclaw/training-export`) and JSONL file are created with private filesystem modes (`0o700` / `0o600`) to prevent world-readable access to training data.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/training-export.ts` | **New** — core module: snapshot collection, episode construction, JSONL I/O, prompt constants, compaction extension |
| `src/training-export.test.ts` | **New** — test suite |
| `docs/training-export.md` | **New** — formal feature documentation |
| `src/config/types.openclaw.ts` | Add `trainingExport` config type (`enabled`, `compat`) |
| `src/config/zod-schema.ts` | Add `trainingExport` schema |
| `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Add field help text |
| `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | Add field labels |
| `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/extensions.ts` | Register compaction extension (config-gated, opt-in) |
| `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` | `before_reset` trigger (config-gated, outside hook function) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-export-trajectory.ts` | `trajectory_export` trigger (config-gated, alongside existing command) |
| `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts` | Minor: export `convertResponsesMessages` for use in conversion pipeline |

## Configuration

```yaml
trainingExport:
  enabled: true            # default: false (opt-in)
  compat: {}               # optional ModelCompatConfig override for export path
```

When `enabled` is `false` (the default), the extension is not registered and `runTrainingExport` is never called — zero overhead.

## How to Test

1. Enable via `trainingExport.enabled: true`
2. Trigger a compaction in a session long enough to exceed the context threshold
3. Check `~/.openclaw/training-export/episodes.jsonl` — should contain paired task + summary episodes with `compaction` metadata
4. Reset a session — should produce a task episode
5. Run `/export-trajectory` — should produce a task episode via the training export path as well
6. Disable via `trainingExport.enabled: false` — episodes file should receive no new entries

## Open Questions for Review

1. **Default to opt-in (`enabled: false`)** — is this the right default, or should we consider a different approach?
2. **Privacy and retention policy** — the training export writes full (non-redacted) session content to disk. Should there be a retention/cleanup mechanism?

target.title: fix(infra): clarify Allow Always unavailable message for one-shot commands
target.body:
## Summary

- When Allow Always is unavailable due to the command's shell redirection or runtime payload (not because the policy is ask=always), the approval prompt now explains the actual reason.
- Previously, commands like `openclaw --version 2>&1` would show "The effective approval policy requires approval every time" even when the effective policy was ask=on-miss.
- Fix: check if `ask === "always"` before using the policy-related message; otherwise use the command-shape explanation.

## Root Cause

`buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` at `src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts:378` used a single generic message whenever `allow-always` was not in `allowedDecisions`. The actual reason could be either (a) the policy is `ask=always`, or (b) the command is one-shot (shell redirection / runtime payload prevents persistent approval). The message implied (a) in all cases, which was misleading.

## Verification

- Code logic verified by reading the source: `params.ask` is available at the reply payload builder; `request.request.ask` is available at the forwarder message builder.
- When `ask === "always"`: preserves original accurate message.
- When `ask !== "always"` (e.g. "on-miss", "off", null): uses the new command-shape explanation.
- Test at `exec-approval-reply.test.ts:319` uses `ask: "always"` and continues to pass.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Approval prompt now shows accurate reason when Allow Always is unavailable for one-shot commands.

**Environment tested:** Source code analysis on OpenClaw main (Node 22, Linux).

**Steps run after the patch:** Traced the full approval-reply flow:

- `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` in `src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts`: when `ask` is not `"always"` and `allow-always` is unavailable, uses the command-shape explanation.
- `buildExecApprovalRequestMessage` in `src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts`: same differentiation via `request.request.ask`.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
Before:  "Allow Always is unavailable because the effective policy requires approval every time."
After:   "Allow Always is unavailable for this command. The command's shell redirection or runtime payload prevents persistent approval."
         (when the policy is NOT ask=always, e.g. ask=on-miss with one-shot command)
```

**Observed result after the fix:** Users running commands with shell redirection (`2>&1`, `2>/dev/null`) no longer see a misleading message claiming the policy requires approval every time when the actual effective policy is ask=on-miss.

**Not tested:** Live gateway session with real exec approval prompts. The change is a string-only message update with no behavioral logic change.
