target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) introduced `allowBootstrap: true` in heartbeat delivery-target resolution so plugin channel targets could be loaded on demand. However, `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause

`bootstrapAttempts` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts`:
- **Success**: key cached → subsequent ticks skip
- **Failure** (plugin not installed / config issue): key deleted → every tick re-scans

## Changes

1. **Hot path**: heartbeat call sites pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`
2. **Startup pre-activation**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` loads external plugins once before heartbeat loop
3. **Per-agent coverage**: iterates `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` merge semantics)
4. **Session-derived `target:last`**: keeps guarded bootstrap (not pre-activatable from config)
5. **Hot reload & override preactivation**: `updateConfig` and `requestHeartbeat` (cron/manual wakes) call preactivation so externally-configured targets introduced after startup are covered
6. **Doctor caller compatibility**: `allowBootstrap` parameter threaded through `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` so doctor (which runs outside the wake loop) can resolve external plugin targets without preactivation
7. **Test coverage**: mock-backed assertions in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` verifying external-target resolution, standard-channel skip, dedup, and distinct-target branches

## Evidence

### Test proof

```
pnpm test src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
```
131/131 tests pass across 3 test files (19 + 87 + 25).

### Real gateway proof

Production config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`), heartbeat `every=30s target=qqbot`, no `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` — real gateway process with qqbot/feishu channels connected.

Gateway startup:
```
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] http server listening (12 plugins…)
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] ready
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [heartbeat] started
```

Proof event timeline (appendFileSync probes, reverted from source before commit):
```
[gateway]  pre-activate: target=qqbot isExternal=false  → standard channel no-op 1ms
[heartbeat] main-plugin resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] session-route resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] TICK COMPLETE: agent=test_agent channel=qqbot to=proof-test-target totalMs=3
```

## Revision (2026-07-06)

Addressed ClawSweeper review findings:

- **P1 — reload gap**: `updateConfig()` in heartbeat runner now calls `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` before rebuilding the agent schedule
- **P1 — override gap**: `requestHeartbeat()` wake handler pre-activates requested-heartbeat override targets before the no-bootstrap resolver runs
- **P1 — doctor regression**: `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` accepts `allowBootstrap?: boolean` so the doctor path (which runs outside the wake loop without preactivation) can still resolve external plugin targets
- **Test assertions**: `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` now uses mocked `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` with real assertions (call count, `allowBootstrap: true`, standard-channel skip, dedup)
- Kept existing `target:last` guarded bootstrap unchanged

## Revision (2026-07-07) #1

Removed duplicate heartbeat plugin preactivation path identified by ClawSweeper review:

- **P2 — duplicate startup preactivation**: Removed `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` from `activateGatewayScheduledServices`. The `startHeartbeatRunner` constructor already calls `updateConfig(state.cfg)` which handles the initial preactivation plus all hot-reload/config-update paths. Removing the gateway-side call eliminates a repeated registry scan when an external target fails to load.
- Updated comment in `heartbeat-runner.ts` `updateConfig` to reflect it is now the single preactivation path.
- 147 related tests pass (`server-runtime-services.test.ts`, `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, `targets.test.ts`).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #2 (a0ba292)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — gating preactivation to enabled, deliverable heartbeat configs:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` was called from `updateConfig` before the interval filter (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs`). A disabled heartbeat config (`every: "0m"`) with an external target still triggered `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` during startup/reload, scanning all installed plugins unnecessarily. External targets without a recipient (`to`) were also preactivated even though the runner can never deliver to them.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Config-scan path (startup/reload): each target is only preactivated when the heartbeat is enabled (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` returns non-null) AND has a deliverable recipient (`to` is set). This mirrors the `updateConfig` scheduling loop which skips agents with `intervalMs === 0`.
- Direct heartbeat override path (cron/manual wakes via `requestHeartbeat`): still preactivates without an interval check because the caller already validated the wake is active. Only skips targets without a recipient.

**New regression tests** (+7 in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`):
- ✅ Disabled default (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Disabled per-agent (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on default target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on per-agent target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on heartbeat override → no preactivation
- ✅ Per-agent with its own `every: "15m"` overrides disabled default → preactivated

**Test results**: 19/19 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass.

## Revision (2026-07-07) #3 (1334dd29)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — skip default target preactivation when explicit per-agent heartbeats override scheduling:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` unconditionally added `agents.defaults.heartbeat` to the target set even when `agents.list[]` entries had their own heartbeat configs. In that case `resolveHeartbeatAgents` schedules only the merged per-agent entries — it does not schedule the default as a standalone target. Preactivating the unused default target caused an unnecessary full-plugin-registry scan on startup/reload.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Added a `hasExplicitAgents` check mirroring `resolveHeartbeatAgents`: when any `agents.list[]` entry has a `heartbeat` block, the standalone default target is skipped. Only the per-agent effective targets (which may merge `target` or `to` from defaults) are preactivated.
- When no agent has an explicit heartbeat, the default target is still preactivated as before (it is what the scheduler runs).

**Updated tests** (+1 new regression, 2 existing tests adjusted):
- ✅ New: "skips the default external target when a per-agent heartbeat overrides it" — default `unused-external-plugin` with `to: room:default` is not preactivated because agent `override-agent` has its own `background-channel` target
- ✅ Adjusted: "pre-activates distinct external targets from defaults and per-agent configs" → now expects only the per-agent target (default skipped)
- ✅ Adjusted: "pre-activates a per-agent external target that inherits to from defaults" → now expects only the per-agent target with inherited `to` (default skipped)

**Test results**: 21/21 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass (133 total).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #4 — fix external-target detector (9db74edf)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — `isExternalPluginTarget` used wrong helper semantics:

**Problem**: `isExternalPluginTarget` used `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` and inverted its return value to decide "external plugin." But `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` preserves unknown plugin ids as deliverable (for external-plugin routing), so an explicit external target like `external-channel` made the helper return a truthy value and `isExternalPluginTarget` returned `false` — silently skipping bootstrap preactivation for external plugin targets.

**Root cause in the contract**:
- `normalizeMessageChannel` (in `message-channel-core.ts:27`) preserves unknown-but-normalized ids: `return normalizeAnyChannelId(normalized) ?? normalized`
- `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` wraps `normalizeMessageChannel` + `isDeliverableMessageChannel`, so it returns a truthy value for unknown external plugin channels
- The old `isExternalPluginTarget` inverted this: `return !normalized` — wrong, because the helper returned a value for external channels

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Replaced `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` + `normalizeChatChannelId`
- `isDeliverableMessageChannel(rawTarget)` confirms the target is a deliverable channel id (non-internal, non-empty)
- `!normalizeChatChannelId(rawTarget)` confirms it's NOT a built-in chat channel — built-in channels are already in the bundled catalog and don't need bootstrap
- Only targets that pass both checks (deliverable but not built-in) are classified as external plugin targets

**Updated tests** — `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`:
- Replaced `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` mock with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` + `normalizeChatChannelId` mocks
- `isDeliverableMessageChannel` now returns `true` for any non-empty string (matching real contract: unknown plugin ids are deliverable)
- `normalizeChatChannelId` only returns non-null for built-in channel ids (`telegram`, `discord`, `whatsapp`)
- This means external plugin targets (e.g. `external-channel`) correctly pass `isExternalPluginTarget` — deliverable but not built-in → needs preactivation
- Built-in channel targets (e.g. `telegram`) correctly fail `isExternalPluginTarget` — deliverable AND built-in → skip preactivation

**Test results**: 22/22 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass (136 total).



## Revision (2026-07-08)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — explicit normalized heartbeat plugin targets not honoring caller `allowBootstrap`:

**Problem**: When `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel` preserves an external plugin channel id (production normalization contract at `message-channel-core.ts:27-29`), the explicit target reaches the later plugin lookup at `targets.ts:217-225`. That lookup hardcoded `allowBootstrap: isSessionDerived` (always `false` for explicit targets) and `allowBundledFallback: !isSessionDerived` (always `true` for explicit targets). This meant:
- Doctor's `allowBootstrap: true` was ignored → false "replies are dropped silently" warnings for external plugin heartbeat targets
- Bundled fallback was enabled on the heartbeat hot path → could lazy-load bundled channel module code contrary to the performance boundary

**Fix in `targets.ts`**:
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget`: plugin lookup now honors `params.allowBootstrap` for explicit targets (`isSessionDerived || params.allowBootstrap === true`) and disables bundled fallback unconditionally (`allowBundledFallback: false`)
- `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTargetWithSessionRoute`: bundled fallback also disabled in sync with the primary resolution path

**New regression tests** (+2 in `targets.test.ts`):
- ✅ Doctor `allowBootstrap: true` passes through for explicit external targets preserved by production normalization
- ✅ Hot path keeps `allowBootstrap: false` with bundled fallback disabled
- Both tests override the normalization mock to simulate production behavior where external plugin ids are preserved (rather than returning `undefined`)

**Test results**: 89/89 `targets.test.ts`, 22/22 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, 7/7 `doctor-heartbeat-session-target.test.ts` — all pass (145 total).


## Revision (2026-07-08) #2 — fix CI lint (9a37f344)

Fixed `check-lint` CI failure (2 `eslint/curly` violations in `targets.test.ts`):

**Problem**: Two newly added test helpers in revision #1 used single-line `if (cond) return val;` without braces — a style rule enforced by `eslint/curly` in CI.

**Fix in `targets.test.ts`**: Added braces to both `if` statements (lines 987, 1026):
```ts
if (normalized === "ext-plugin") {
  return normalized;
}
```

**Test results**: 145/145 pass across 4 test files. `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean.


## Revision (2026-07-08) — external plugin proof

Real gateway proof with a minimal external channel plugin (`proof-channel`, `deliveryMode: "gateway"`, registered via `openclaw.plugin.json` `channels: ["proof-channel"]`). The plugin is NOT bundled — it lives under `~/.openclaw/extensions/proof-channel/` and is discovered at runtime.

### Setup

- Added `proof-channel` channel plugin to `~/.openclaw/extensions/proof-channel/` (CJS, `deliveryMode: "gateway"`, no bundled fallback)
- Configured `test_agent` with `heartbeat: { target: "proof-channel", to: "proof-test-recipient", every: "30s" }`
- Enabled `proof-channel` in `plugins.entries`
- Added temporary `appendFileSync` probes to capture the preactivation→delivery sequence (reverted before push)

### Gateway startup log

```
[gateway] loading configuration…
[gateway] resolving authentication…
[gateway] starting...
[gateway] starting HTTP server...
[health-monitor] started (interval: 300s, startup-grace: 60s, channel-connect-grace: 120s)
[plugins] proof-channel: loaded without install/load-path provenance; treat as untracked local code.
[heartbeat] started
```

### Proof event timeline

| Phase | Timestamp (UTC) | Event |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| Startup | `02:23:10.748Z` | `preactivate-start` — `hasOverride: false` (config-scan path) |
| Startup | `02:23:10.750Z` | `preactivate-config` — target=`proof-channel`, `targetCount=1`, calls `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` |
| Tick #1 | `02:23:22.678Z` | `heartbeat-delivery` — target=`proof-channel`, `allowBootstrap: false`, `pluginResolved: true`, `hadPreparedPlugin: false` |
| Tick #2 | `02:24:13.197Z` | `heartbeat-delivery` — target=`proof-channel`, `allowBootstrap: false`, `pluginResolved: true`, `hadPreparedPlugin: false` |

### Key observations

1. **Preactivation done once** — `preactivate-start` fires once at startup (config-scan path). The external plugin target `proof-channel` is resolved with `allowBootstrap: true`, loading it into the active registry.

2. **Hot path stays bootstrap-free** — Both heartbeat ticks deliver with `allowBootstrap: false`. The plugin is already active (`pluginResolved: true`) because preactivation loaded it.

3. **ZERO bootstrap-heavy events** — `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` was never called on the hot path. The `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry` full-plugin-scan was never triggered during wake ticks. If the old `allowBootstrap: true` behavior were still in place, each tick would have triggered a full registry scan for this external plugin channel.

4. **No bundled fallback** — `hadPreparedPlugin: false` confirms delivery follows the explicit-target path, which disables `allowBundledFallback` — the bundled channel module code is never lazy-loaded from the heartbeat hot path.

### Environment

- OS: Linux (x86_64), Node 24.13.1
- Branch: `fix/heartbeat-delivery-bootstrap-latency`
- Commit: `9a37f344d49a7da5e182e750238885538aff5eed` (latest PR head)
- Config: production profile (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) + proof plugin + heartbeat override
- Gateway port: 18790

### What was not tested

- Multi-agent heartbeat with mixed bundled/external targets
- Heartbeat delivery during plugin reload (`updateConfig` hot-reload path)
- Requested heartbeat override wake path (cron/manual wakes with external targets)
- Production external plugins (qqbot, feishu) — proof used a minimal no-network plugin to isolate the registry/preactivation behavior



## Revision (2026-07-08) — normalize target before preactivation classification (d5b03d3)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] finding — `isExternalPluginTarget` checked raw heartbeat target with `isDeliverableMessageChannel` without prior normalization:

**Problem**: Config validation accepts heartbeat targets case-insensitively by lowercasing installed plugin channel ids before membership checks (`src/config/validation.ts:1765`). A config `target: "Proof-Channel"` passes validation and delivery later normalizes it to `proof-channel`, but `isDeliverableMessageChannel("Proof-Channel")` returns `false` (it requires already-normalized input per `message-channel-core.ts:36`). The un-normalized mixed-case target was silently skipped, leaving the external plugin un-preloaded — the no-bootstrap hot path then resolved to no target.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- `isExternalPluginTarget` now normalizes the raw target via `normalizeMessageChannel` before calling `isDeliverableMessageChannel` and `normalizeChatChannelId`. This mirrors the config validation contract where installed plugin channel ids are lowercased.
- Imported `normalizeMessageChannel` from `../../utils/message-channel.js` alongside the existing `isDeliverableMessageChannel`.

**New regression test** (+1 in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`):
- ✅ "pre-activates a mixed-case external plugin target" — `target: "Proof-Channel"` is normalized to `proof-channel`, classified as external, and resolved with `allowBootstrap: true`
- Added `normalizeMessageChannel` mock that lowercases input, matching the production contract

**Test results**: 23/23 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 89/89 `targets.test.ts`, 27/27 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, 7/7 `doctor-heartbeat-session-target.test.ts` — all pass (146 total). `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean.

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs

```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:

```

Memory index updated (main).
```

```

[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9

```

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

- Migration needed? (`No`)

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
